title: Epic edge proposal
description: The edge file the epic-dependency-assessor writes for ONE Epic in the dependency-assessment workflow: the candidate <workDir>/candidates/edges.json, which jsonartifact.py validates against this file and publishes as <workDir>/edges.json. `depscore.py validate` then checks it against the tracker and `depscore.py apply-edges` applies it as beads `tracks` edges. Nothing of it is recorded in the matrix. The session runs no `put`, no `link` and no apply. The edge test and the foundation checklist are the agent-teams-workforce:epic-sequencing skill's. The owner runs this workflow; the order of every Epic is computed by scripts/portfolio/epicorder.py, whose --apply replaces the owned edges this file sets.

edges.description: EVERY edge to or from the assessed Epic that passes the edge test, each owned standing edge it keeps included, and no edge that does not touch it.

withdrawn.description: Every owned standing edge (the context's `standing` with `owned: true`) that `edges` does not keep. An edge with `owned: false` is in neither list.

Edge.description: One architecture dependency: an architecture decision `to` rests on should be designed from `from`'s requirements first, and the matrix does not hold that decision approved. `from` is elaborated before `to`; both are Epics.

from.description: The beads id of the Epic whose requirements should drive the decision.

to.description: The beads id of the Epic that rests on the decision.

reason.description: The architecture decision and whose requirements should drive it, in one line.

archCheck.description: The matrix entry id (with the document heading, for a document) that states the decision this edge orders, and that the matrix does not hold it approved; or that the lookup returned nothing. Only the `approved` flag, an Epic's elaboration having approved the decision, removes the need for the edge: an entry existing or a document at `lifecycle: effective` does not, because every document still iterates with each Epic (epic-sequencing). An edge without it is refused.

answers.description: Required only on an edge the context's `withdrawn` list covers: why the recorded withdrawal reason is wrong, on the architecture. Without it that edge is refused.
